name: Phalanx Systems GripShadow Infiltration Glove
description:
Street-sourced from a Phalanx Systems secondary label — technically discontinued, practically everywhere in the right circles. Thin-profile neoprene-analog shell with a microsuction gecko-pad palm and finger surface for adhesion on glass, smooth ferrocrete, and lacquered metal. The outer surface is electrostatically neutral, defeating most friction-based print scanners. Interior is smooth enough to prevent secondary print transfer.

Fingers are full-length but the tips are slit with a pull-tab system — fold them back for unmediated touch, snap them forward for full coverage. No branding visible externally. The only identifier is a small embossed triangle inside the left cuff.
functionality: Microsuction palm and fingers provide adhesion on smooth vertical surfaces; electrostatic neutral coat defeats friction-print scanners; pull-tab fingertip system allows rapid switch between full coverage and bare-tip tactile access; no external branding.
what_it_says: You go places you weren't invited and you don't leave evidence.
story_hooks: A security consultant finds GripShadow microsuction residue on a 40th-floor window — whoever made the climb didn't use a rig.
The embossed triangle inside the cuff turns out to be a batch code that traces back to a single production run sold to one buyer three years ago.
A Tier 3 accountant is found wearing a pair — which raises more questions than the missing files ever did.
